In a population characterized by highly prevalent maternal obesity, fetal abdominal circumference-guidance of GDM therapy can limit excess macrosomy and LGA.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of fetal abdominal circumference as an adjunct in the management of gestational diabetes is a reasonable and effective strategy in a population with high rates of maternal obesity and gestational weight gains.

ultrasound-guided therapy of maternal diabetes, in general clinic practice, can limit excess fetal macrosomia and large for gestational size (LGA) and is effective in a population with maternal obesity.
ultrasound-guided therapy of obesity-related GDM is a feasible and effective method of care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ultrasound-guided therapy of maternal diabetes is a useful tool for the obstetrician to limit excess fetal growth, especially in the context of obesity.
ultrasound-guided therapy is effective in the outpatient setting and that it is effective in a highly obese population.
fetal ultrasound is a useful adjunct to the care of obese women with GDM.
The main takeaway from our work is that

fetal abdominal circumference-guidance of GDM management in an outpatient setting can be effective in preventing macrosomia and other neonatal complications in a population characterized by highly prevalent maternal obesity.
ultrasound-guided therapy of maternal obesity is a safe and efficacious approach to GDM management, and that it can be successfully applied in a clinical, rather than a research, setting.
fetal abdominal circumference-guidance can be used to optimize glycemic targets for GDM patients in an outpatient setting.
